title: Fix it: update a status field without rebuilding the whole object
prompt:
The script in the editor is **almost** right. It passes on the sample and fails on a case you cannot see.

The original task was:

You have objects with a `status` field and various other fields. For each object, set the status to `"inactive"`, but keep every other field exactly as it was.

Some objects might not have a `status` field at all. These should be left unchanged (since you cannot update a field that does not exist).

Find what is wrong and fix it. You can press Run to see what it currently does.
hints: Run it on the sample first. If the sample looks right, the bug only shows on data the sample does not contain.
Ask what kind of input would break this — an empty list, a missing field, a value ordered differently.
tries to update a field that does not exist

explanation.approach: The `update` operator modifies one or more fields in an object while leaving the rest intact. It only works on fields that already exist. If you ask it to update a field that is not there, it silently does nothing — which is the trap.

snippets.label: The basic update syntax
snippets.note: The `status` field changed to `inactive`, but `id` and `name` stayed the same. The `update` left everything else untouched.

snippets.label: What happens when you update a missing field
snippets.note: The `update` did not add a `missing` field. It only modifies fields that already exist. This is the trap: the operation succeeds silently, but nothing happened.

snippets.label: Iterating with map and update together
snippets.note: Each element of the array gets the update applied. Both items now have `status: "inactive"`, and all other fields stayed the same.

snippets.label: An object with no status field
snippets.note: Since this object has no `status` field, the `update` does nothing. Both `id` and `priority` are unchanged. This is why the trap matters: the missing field silently breaks the logic.

snippets.label: Multiple case branches in one update
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
{id: 1, status: "active", priority: 1} update {
  case .status -> "inactive"
  case .priority -> 99
}
snippets.note: You can update multiple fields at once by listing multiple `case` statements. Both `status` and `priority` changed.

snippets.label: Why update is better than rebuilding
snippets.note: With `update`, you specify only what changes. If someone adds a new field to this object later, your code still works. If you had hand-rebuilt it with explicit fields, the new field would be lost.
